AI Overviews & AI Mode

Google AI Optimization Services

Google AI Optimization improves a website’s eligibility to appear in and be cited by Google’s AI-powered search features, AI Overviews and AI Mode, by applying the same fundamentals Google’s own documentation says those features rely on: crawlable, indexable pages, useful and original content, accurate structured data, sound page experience, and clear internal linking. It is for businesses that rank in classic results but are absent from the AI answer above them. There is no separate AI ranking system to optimize for, and Fix Website Issues does not pretend otherwise; this is technical SEO and content quality work, delivered within a broader AI search optimization practice.

Aligned With Google Search Central Guidance | Search Console Driven | Technical SEO First | Houston-Based, Nationwide Since 2013

Request an AI Visibility Audit
Call 832-266-7209
What Google says AI features rely on
No special markup or separate optimization required, per Google Search Central.
✓Crawlable and indexable pages
✓Unique, valuable content for people
✓Good page experience
✓Structured data that matches visible content
✓High-quality images and video, indexable
✓Content controls: snippet and preview settings
Measured in Search Console: AI feature traffic is reported within Web search performance.
Addresses

Absent From AI Overviews

Ranking in classic results while a competitor is cited in the AI answer above them.

Basis

Google’s Own Guidance

Everything here maps to Google Search Central documentation, not to speculation about a hidden AI algorithm.

Method

Fix, Then Improve

Crawl, index, and rendering problems first; then content depth, structure, and internal links.

Measurement

Search Console + Observation

Performance data from Search Console, plus recorded AI Overview and AI Mode checks for your query set.

What Is Google AI Optimization?

Google AI Optimization is the work of making a website eligible for, and a strong candidate to be cited in, Google’s AI-powered search experiences, AI Overviews and AI Mode, by meeting the crawling, indexing, content-quality, structured-data, and page-experience standards Google publishes for Search generally. Google’s documentation on AI features is explicit that these experiences use the same core systems as Search and that no additional or special requirements exist. Optimizing for them means doing Search fundamentals unusually well and then making sure your pages are the clearest, most useful source for the queries where AI answers appear.

Two things follow from that. First, a site with crawl blocks, thin or duplicated content, misleading structured data, or slow, unstable pages is unlikely to be surfaced in an AI Overview no matter what else is done. Second, the tactics sold as “AI Overview hacks” (special files, special schema, keyword-stuffed summaries) are not supported by anything Google has published. We do not offer them. We do offer the technical and content work Google describes, executed by a team that repairs broken sites for a living.

How AI Overviews and AI Mode choose what to show

Google states that AI features draw on its search index and ranking systems, may run several related queries behind the scenes, and link to supporting pages so users can learn more. Pages that answer a query directly, contain unique value, and come from a site Google already trusts are the natural candidates. The user’s location, query wording, language, and Google’s own decisions about when to show an AI answer all affect the result, which is why we speak of eligibility, not placement.

Where this fits

Google AI Optimization is the Google-specific application of the fundamentals. For cross-platform citation work see Generative Engine Optimization; for ChatGPT specifically see ChatGPT SEO; for question-level content structure see Answer Engine Optimization. All of them begin with the AI Visibility Audit.

Signs your site may need this

  • AI Overviews appear for your main queries and never cite you.
  • Search Console shows impressions dropping while average position holds.
  • Key pages are excluded from the index or flagged for rendering issues.
  • Structured data errors or markup that describes content not on the page.
  • Location or service pages that are templated near-duplicates.
  • Core Web Vitals failing on mobile.

Who Google AI Optimization Is For

Any business that depends on Google for customers is affected by AI Overviews and AI Mode. The businesses that benefit most from a dedicated effort share one trait: they already have organic visibility to protect or extend.

Businesses whose organic traffic is eroding while rankings hold. This pattern usually means an AI answer is now satisfying the query above your listing. The response is to become a cited source in that answer rather than a link below it.

Local and multi-location service businesses. AI Overviews for “best,” “near me,” and “how much” queries lean on business information Google already trusts: Business Profile, consistent listings, and location pages with real, distinct content.

Medical, legal, and financial sites. Google applies higher standards to these topics. Sites with clear authorship, credentials, accurate schema, and original content are more likely to be surfaced; thin, unattributed content is not.

Ecommerce. Product pages with accurate, complete structured data, original descriptions, and indexable images are the candidates for AI-assisted shopping answers.

Sites recovering from technical problems. Migrations, redesigns, hacks, and plugin conflicts leave crawl and index damage that silently disqualifies pages. Repairing that is where we start; see our SEO repair services.

Google AI Optimization vs traditional SEO

They are the same discipline. Google AI Optimization is traditional SEO with two emphases: content that can be lifted as a supporting source (specific, self-contained, verifiable passages) and a measurement approach that watches AI feature presence, not just position.

When something else comes first

A hacked or broken site is repaired first; see hacked website repair and WordPress error repair. If your concern spans ChatGPT, Copilot, and Perplexity as well as Google, the umbrella AI Search Optimization program is the broader fit. If you do not know where you stand, the AI Visibility Audit comes first.

Problems Google AI Optimization Solves

Each problem below maps to a documented Google requirement, and each fix is something we implement rather than recommend.

Problem

Pages Google cannot fully crawl or render

Blocked resources, script-only content, soft 404s, redirect chains. Fix: crawl and render diagnostics, robots and resource fixes, server-rendered text, clean index coverage in Search Console.

Problem

Content that adds nothing unique

Rewritten manufacturer copy, generic service descriptions, AI-generated filler. Fix: original content that reflects first-hand experience, specifics, and clear authorship, in line with Google’s helpful-content guidance.

Problem

Structured data that misleads

Markup describing content not on the page, invalid types, or errors in Search Console. Fix: validated schema that matches the visible page, removal of unsupported markup, monitoring of the enhancements reports.

Problem

Poor page experience

Failing Core Web Vitals, intrusive interstitials, layout shift, non-HTTPS. Fix: performance, stability, and mobile usability work at the theme, plugin, and hosting level.

Problem

Weak internal linking and site structure

Important pages buried, orphaned, or competing with each other. Fix: topic clustering, descriptive internal links, consolidation of duplicates, and an architecture Google can follow.

Problem

Images and video Google cannot index

Missing alt text, images injected by script, video without markup or a page of its own. Fix: indexable media with descriptive alt text, image sitemaps, and VideoObject markup where warranted.

What Is Included in Google AI Optimization

Every deliverable traces to a Google Search Central recommendation. Technical work is done by the team that provides website maintenance and repair, so fixes are applied directly.

Crawling and indexing

  • Technical SEO audit: robots, sitemaps, canonicals, redirects, status codes
  • Rendering verification with URL Inspection
  • Index coverage cleanup in Search Console
  • Duplicate and near-duplicate consolidation
  • Crawl budget and log review for large sites

Content quality

  • Content quality review against Google’s helpful-content questions
  • Service and location page rewrites with unique, specific value
  • Passage-level structure so key answers stand on their own
  • Authorship, credentials, and about-page clarity
  • Content consolidation and pruning

Structured data, media, and experience

  • Schema validation and correction; removal of unsupported markup
  • Organization, LocalBusiness, Product, Article, and Person schema where content supports it
  • Image and video indexability, alt text, media sitemaps
  • Core Web Vitals and mobile usability fixes
  • Internal linking and site architecture

Measurement

  • Search Console performance analysis by query and page
  • Recorded AI Overview and AI Mode checks for a fixed query set
  • Google Business Profile and local consistency review
  • Monthly reporting on index health, performance, and AI feature observations

How We Evaluate a Site for Google’s AI Features

The evaluation follows Google’s published checklist in order: can it be crawled, is it indexed, is it useful, is it accurate, is it fast, is it connected. Then we look at which queries trigger AI answers and who is cited.

Start With an AI Visibility Audit
  1. Crawlability. Robots rules, blocked resources, status codes, redirect chains, sitemap accuracy.
  2. Indexability and rendering. Index coverage report, URL Inspection on key pages, script-dependent content.
  3. Search Console performance. Queries, pages, and trends; impressions vs. clicks vs. position to spot AI-answer displacement.
  4. AI feature observation. A fixed query set checked for AI Overviews and AI Mode; cited sources recorded.
  5. Content quality. Originality, depth, first-hand experience, authorship, and passage clarity against Google’s guidance.
  6. Structured data. Validity, match to visible content, enhancement report errors.
  7. Page experience. Core Web Vitals, mobile usability, HTTPS, interstitials.
  8. Media. Image and video indexability, alt text, sitemaps, markup.
  9. Site structure and links. Clusters, orphaned pages, cannibalization, descriptive anchors.
  10. Local and entity signals. Business Profile, consistency of name, address, phone, and schema across the web.

How Google AI Optimization Works

Step 1 — Baseline in Search Console

Export performance by query and page, note where impressions are rising while clicks fall, and record AI Overview and AI Mode presence and cited sources for the priority query set.

Step 2 — Repair crawling, indexing, and rendering

Fix everything that keeps Google from fully reading the site. This is repair work, and it is where most of the immediate gains come from.

Step 3 — Correct structured data and page experience

Validate schema, remove markup that does not match the page, and resolve Core Web Vitals and mobile issues at the source.

Step 4 — Improve content where it matters

Rewrite the pages tied to AI-answer queries so they contain original, specific, self-contained passages with clear authorship and evidence, following Google’s people-first content guidance.

Step 5 — Connect the site

Build topic clusters, add descriptive internal links, consolidate competing pages, and make media indexable.

Step 6 — Re-measure and iterate

Monthly Search Console review and AI feature checks. Pages that gain citations tell us what to replicate; pages that do not are revisited.

How Fix Website Issues Approaches Google’s AI Features

We read Google’s documentation, not rumors about it. Every recommendation on this page corresponds to a Search Central page we can point to. When Google says no special markup is needed, we do not sell special markup.

Displacement shows up in Search Console first. The clearest sign that AI answers are affecting a site is impressions holding or rising while clicks fall on the same queries. We look for that pattern before anything else, because it tells us which queries to prioritize.

Repair precedes optimization. Our clients often arrive after a migration or plugin conflict silently deindexed half the site. Content work on unindexed pages is wasted; we fix the foundation first and can show the before-and-after in the coverage report.

Content controls are respected. If a client wants to limit how their content appears in AI features, Google’s snippet and preview controls exist for that, and we implement them rather than argue.

Google AI Optimization vs Traditional SEO

One discipline, two emphases. The table shows where the attention shifts.

AreaTraditional SEOGoogle AI Optimization
GoalRank in the ten blue linksBe eligible for and cited in AI Overviews and AI Mode, while still ranking
Systems involvedGoogle's index and ranking systemsThe same systems; no separate AI ranking algorithm exists
Content emphasisPage-level relevance for keywordsSelf-contained, specific, verifiable passages with clear authorship
Structured dataFor rich resultsSame purpose; accuracy matters, no AI-specific schema exists
MeasurementPosition, clicksSearch Console performance (AI traffic included in Web totals) plus recorded AI feature observations
LimitationsRankings do not guarantee an AI citationGoogle does not report AI Overview citations separately; whether an AI answer appears is Google's decision

What Google AI Optimization Cannot Guarantee

  • Whether Google shows an AI Overview or AI Mode answer for a query is Google’s decision and varies by query, location, language, and user.
  • Which pages Google cites in an AI answer is not controllable by any agency.
  • Google does not report AI Overview citations as a separate metric; AI feature traffic is included in Web totals in Search Console.
  • No special file, schema type, or markup is required for AI features, and none causes inclusion.
  • The work improves eligibility, quality, and clarity. Placements, rankings, traffic, or leads cannot be promised.
Example methodology, not a case study

How We Would Approach a Typical Home Services Company

Situation. A plumbing company in a large metro ranks in the top five for its main service queries, but Search Console shows clicks down over six months on the same queries while impressions are flat. AI Overviews now appear for most of them, citing a national lead-generation site and a manufacturer’s page.

Likely findings. Service pages are 200-word templates with the city name swapped; a caching plugin serves Googlebot a stale, script-heavy version; LocalBusiness schema lists a phone number the company stopped using; Core Web Vitals fail on mobile because of an oversized hero video; no page answers the “how much” and “how long” questions the AI answers address.

Sequence. Fix caching and rendering; correct schema; replace the hero video with an optimized image (week 1). Rewrite the six highest-impression service pages with real pricing ranges, timelines, process, and a named licensed plumber’s authorship (weeks 2 to 5). Build a cluster of question pages linked from the services. Align Business Profile and listings. Re-measure monthly.

Measurement. Search Console clicks and impressions on the query set, index coverage, Core Web Vitals field data, and recorded AI Overview citations. This is structure, not a promise of outcome.

Are AI Overviews Taking Your Google Traffic?

We can read your Search Console data for the displacement pattern, check whether Google can fully crawl and render your pages, and record which sources it cites for your queries, before proposing anything.

Why a Repair-First Team for Google’s AI Features

Fix Website Issues is the website repair and technical SEO division of WevTEC, Houston-based and serving businesses nationwide since 2013. Google’s AI features reward the fundamentals, and the fundamentals are what we have spent over a decade fixing on sites that were broken, hacked, migrated badly, or slowed to a crawl by plugins.

  • Crawl, index, and rendering diagnostics are daily work, with Search Console evidence for every fix.
  • Implementation on WordPress, WooCommerce, and custom sites, including theme, plugin, and hosting-level performance work.
  • Structured data done honestly: validated, matched to visible content, removed when it is not.
  • Content work grounded in Google’s helpful-content guidance, with clinical, legal, and financial pages reviewed by the client before publishing.
  • No invented AI algorithms, no special files, no guarantees.

Who is accountable

Strategy and implementation are handled by the Fix Website Issues technical SEO team under WevTEC. This page was last updated September 2026. More about the team.

What is Google AI Optimization?

Google AI Optimization is the work of making a website eligible for, and a strong candidate to be cited in, Google’s AI Overviews and AI Mode by meeting the crawling, indexing, content-quality, structured-data, and page-experience standards Google publishes for Search generally.

Is there a separate AI ranking algorithm to optimize for?

No. Google’s documentation states that AI features use the same core systems as Search and that no additional or special requirements exist. Anyone selling optimization for a separate AI ranking algorithm is selling something Google has said does not exist.

Do I need special schema for AI Overviews?

No. Google requires no special markup for AI features. Accurate structured data that matches the visible page helps Google understand content, as it always has. Markup that describes content not on the page can hurt.

How do I measure AI Overview traffic?

Traffic from AI Overviews and AI Mode is included in the Web search type in Search Console performance reports, not broken out separately. We combine that data with recorded observations of which sources appear for a fixed query set.

Can you guarantee my site appears in AI Overviews?

No. Whether Google shows an AI answer and which pages it cites is Google’s decision and varies by query, location, and user. We improve eligibility and quality and report what changes; we do not promise placements.

Can I control how my content appears in AI features?

Yes. Google’s preview controls, including nosnippet and max-snippet, apply to AI features as they do to snippets. If you want to limit how your content appears, we implement those controls. Note that they can also reduce visibility.

What kind of pages get cited in AI Overviews?

Pages that answer a query directly, contain unique value, come from a site Google already trusts, and are fully crawlable and indexable. Rankings help but do not guarantee a citation.

How do I know if AI Overviews are affecting my traffic?

Check Search Console for queries where impressions hold or rise while clicks fall. That pattern often means an AI answer is satisfying the query above your listing. We look for it first because it shows which queries to prioritize.

How does this differ from GEO or ChatGPT SEO?

Google AI Optimization focuses on Google’s AI features using Google’s published guidance. GEO covers citation across many platforms, and ChatGPT SEO focuses on OpenAI’s products. They share the same foundation and are usually combined.

How long does it take?

Technical fixes take effect after Google re-crawls, usually within days to weeks. Content improvements take longer to be reflected. AI feature presence is observed monthly; timing varies and is not guaranteed.
